title: Numbers 21 — Chormah (Hormah), the serpent of bronze, the march around Moab, and the defeat of Sichon (Sihon) and Og

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: dereḵ hāʾăṯārîm 'the way of Atarim' follows the MT, with the versional 'the spies' recorded (MT-baseline policy). 'The Negev' follows genesis-woh. Non-blocking: check the locator 'Herzog, in Arad I, 1984'. The standard report is Herzog et al., 'The Israelite Fortress at Arad', BASOR 254 (1984).

Re-parsed wəhaḥăramtî ʾeṯ-ʿārêhem (Hiphil of ḥrm). The ASV 'utterly destroy' is defensible but loses the root, while 18:14 renders the noun 'devoted thing' and Chormah plays on the verb. The parallel joshua-woh overlay (herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua) renders the same Hiphil 'devote to destruction' and the noun 'the devoted thing'. That answers the question numbers-woh deferred (F7) and keeps the root visible in English. Proposed: 'then I will devote their cities to destruction.' [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

wayyaḥărēm ʾeṯhem wəʾeṯ-ʿārêhem ... ḥormâ: same issue as v 2. Proposed: 'and they devoted them and their cities to destruction; and the name of the place was called Chormah.' With this rendering the wordplay on Chormah becomes visible to an English reader without a parenthetical gloss, which fits the overlay's no-gloss rule. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

wattiqṣar nep̄eš-hāʿām baddāreḵ: qṣr nep̄eš is an idiom of impatience (Judg 16:16; Zech 11:8). 'The people became impatient' is the idiomatic rendering, and 'by the way to the Sea of Reeds' follows the central entry.

Re-parsed wannîrām ... wannaššîm ʿaḏ-nōp̄aḥ ʾăšer ʿaḏ-mêḏəḇāʾ. The source carries the extraordinary point over the rēš of ʾăšer (checked: U+05C4 present). The note correctly identifies it as one of the ten puncta extraordinaria of the Torah (Sifre Num 69). The line translates the MT ('which reaches to Medeva') as the ASV does, and the Samaritan/LXX 'fire' is recorded.

Re-parsed the single Ketiv/Qere of the wave, ויירש [וַיּוֹרֶשׁ]. Translating the Qere wayyôreš (Hiphil 3ms, 'and he dispossessed') as 'drove out' is correct, and the line is approved. Commentary fix: the note says the Ketiv wyyrš 'is usually vocalized wayyîrəšû' (plural). The consonants have no final waw and can only be the singular Qal wayyîraš 'and he took possession of'. The plural subject the line keeps comes from the preceding wayyilkədû and from the LXX ἐξέβαλον 'they drove out', not from the Ketiv. Correct the note accordingly. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

glossaryReview.reasoning: The convention is philologically sound. Forms are transliterated consistently (tz/q/ch/v/f rules), the ASV equivalence table is complete for the wave, and 'the Egyptians' for the population follows exodus-woh's published practice. claim_type direct is right for a presentation convention. citations: NJPS Deuteronomy (discourses printed without outer marks)
glossaryReview.reasoning: A sound convention. Deut 1:6-4:40 is a single Mosaic discourse, and leaving out the outer marks avoids nesting three levels deep. Checked in the chapter: vv 1-40 unmarked, 4:6 and 4:10 in double marks, 4:41 narration. Embedded speech in Ex 33:5, 12 and Num 18:24, 26, 29-32 is nested correctly. The founder should confirm it before Deut 1-3 and 5 are translated (F8).

Each listed site re-checked in the source. The source carries one Ketiv/Qere (Num 21:32) and one extraordinary point (Num 21:30, U+05C4 over the rēš of ʾăšer). The Deut 4:30 athnach is on hāʾēlleh, and Deut 4:37 has singular suffixes. Every MT reading is construable and the versions are recorded. The only error, the Ketiv vocalization at Num 21:32, is in that verse's commentary, not in this entry.

The clauses are sound and match the exodus-woh and Kings practice (checked: exodus-woh 20:3, 20 'elohim'; 1 Kgs 8:23 'no elohim like you'). One factual fix: the rationale argues that at Deut 4:7 the plural adjective qərōḇîm makes ʾĕlōhîm a class. Plural attributives also stand with ʾĕlōhîm of YHWH himself (Deut 5:26 ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm; Josh 24:19 ʾĕlōhîm qədōšîm; 1 Sam 17:26), so the adjective proves nothing. The comparison 'as YHWH our Elohim' carries the decision. Restate the argument on that basis, in all three overlays and in the DEU-WOH-4:7 commentary. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974)
glossaryReview.reasoning: The scope is correct, and the four idioms (qṣr nep̄eš, nap̄šēnû qāṣâ, the reflexive šmr nep̄eš, the Deuteronomic heart/being pair) are rendered by attested senses. It is consistent with the Kings and Ezekiel rule. exodus-woh 16:16 'souls' is properly left for the next Exodus pass (F10).

The lexical account is accurate. The entry deferred the war-ḥērem rendering to the Former Prophets wave, and that wave now proposes the noun 'the devoted thing' and the Hiphil 'devote to destruction' (Josh 6:17-18, 21; 10:1-40), which keep the root visible in English. Revise the Hiphil clause to 'devote to destruction', changing NUM-WOH-21:2 and 21:3. That makes 18:14 'devoted thing', 21:2-3 and the Chormah wordplay readable as one root, and it allows a single central ḥērem entry. isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban' should be reconciled at the same time. [Resolved at human sign-off, 2026-11-01: the requested fix was applied by the editor.]

reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 253 verses, the 21 overlay entries (18 distinct) and the 43 central ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlays, central base and the parallel diffs before wave-t1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report frames ḥērem (F7) as waiting on the Former Prophets decision. That decision is already visible in joshua-woh's overlay ('devote to destruction'), which confirms the reviewer's revise at Num 21:2-3. The report's list of lexical overlaps with the parallel waves omits ʾărôn (FP1 central aron entry; Ex 25), šôp̄ār (FP1 central shofar entry with a wrong exodus-woh refId) and mitsrayim (isaiah-woh 'Egypt'). These are added under crossDiffCollisions. The report's count of 38 changed English lines was verified line by line, and all 38 are covered by the verdicts.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-proper-names: Option (a) for this wave: keep the split, do not retro-edit signed-off chapters, and record it in the corpus. For the later normalization pass the reviewer recommends one form per name across the corpus. Prefer the transliterated 'Moshe'/'Par'oh', because they are the only English forms left in an otherwise transliterated Torah and the ASV equivalence table already serves readers of the canon's KJV-based English. Prefer the tz spelling 'Mitzrayim', since tz is already the Torah rule for every other tsade. Keep 'the Egyptians' for the population (amend the central gentilic 'Mitsri', which no volume uses), and bring isaiah-woh 'Egypt' into the same decision.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-torah: Retire the transliterated 'torah' at the next Exodus pass and apply the sense rule. Ex 13:9 'the law of YHWH' is a Deuteronomic-style formula (ASV, NRSV 'law'), and Ex 16:4 'my law' (ASV, NRSV) or 'my instruction' (NJPS 'teaching') is a founder preference. Keep Isaiah's 'teaching' as the prophetic clause of the same central entry.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-bara: Agree. Keep 'create' outside Gen 1 (Deut 4:32; Isaiah 40-65 already do), and add a scope sentence to central bara saying that 'shape' is the Gen 1 rendering only.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-teruma: Ratify 'oblation' with hērîm 'set apart'. It is lexically sound, already the corpus term in Ezekiel and Isa 40:20, and it removes the unsupported 'heave' etymology. Semver: minor is defensible because no shipped line changes, but renumber the three parallel 2.84.0 diffs sequentially.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-merism: Confirm 'the heavens and the earth' for the merism outside Gen 1 (exodus-woh 20:11; Deut 4:26, 39). State explicitly that the creation formulas of Isaiah ('created the skies', 'spread out the earth') render the physical sky 'skies', so that the two practices read as one rule.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F6-saraf: The Isaiah wave has already applied the same rule ('a fiery flying serpent' at Isa 14:29; 'seraphim' for the Isa 6 attendants). Promote one central śārāp̄ entry stating both clauses.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F7-herem: The Former Prophets decision is now visible ('devoted thing' / 'devote to destruction'). Adopt it at Num 21:2-3 (reviewer revise), promote a single central ḥērem entry, and reconcile isaiah-woh 43:28 'the ban'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F8-deuteronomy-quotation: Confirm. It matches NJPS practice and the chapter applies it consistently (4:6, 10 inner double marks; 4:41 narration). Apply it unchanged to Deut 1-3 and 5.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F9-kapporet: Keep 'mercy-seat' (ASV, NRSV). It preserves the link with kippēr and Lev 16 that 'cover' loses, and the dispute is fully recorded in the commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F10-next-exodus-pass: Agree with all three items (16:16 'souls'; the 'heavens' register check at 16:4; 17:14; 20:4, 11, 19; 13:9 and 16:4 'torah'). Add the FP1 shofar refId correction (EXO-WOH-20:15, not 20:18) to the merge checklist.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע הַכְּנַעֲנִ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ־עֲרָד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַנֶּ֔גֶב כִּ֚י בָּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הָאֲתָרִ֑ים וַיִּלָּ֙חֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּ֥שְׁבְּ ׀ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שֶֽׁבִי׃

i18n.en: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev, heard that Yisra'el was coming by the way of Atarim; and he fought against Yisra'el and took some of them captive.

notes.official: *hakkənaʿănî meleḵ-ʿărāḏ yōšēḇ hanneḡeḇ* 'the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negev' (ASV 'the South'; 'the Negev' as genesis-woh). Tel Arad has no Late Bronze Age occupation, a known difficulty for the historical setting (Herzog, in *Arad* I, 1984; Levine, *Numbers 21-36*, AB 4B, 2000). *dereḵ hāʾăṯārîm* 'by the way of Atarim' (ASV Atharim): the LXX, the Targums, the Peshitta and the Vulgate read *hattārîm* 'the spies' (cf. 14:6), which many moderns adopt; the line translates the MT and its place name (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). The notice is repeated at 33:40. Names follow `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`, whose table gives the ASV form of every name in the chapter.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נֶ֛דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם־נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֜ן אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְהַֽחֲרַמְתִּ֖י אֶת־עָרֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el vowed a vow to YHWH and said, "If you will indeed give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction."

notes.official: *wayyiddar yiśrāʾēl neḏer laYHWH* 'And Yisra'el vowed a vow to YHWH'. *wəhaḥăramtî ʾeṯ-ʿārêhem* 'then I will devote their cities to destruction' (draft and ASV 'utterly destroy'): the Hiphil of *ḥrm*, to consecrate to YHWH by destruction, rendered so that the root stays visible, as in the joshua-woh overlay for Josh 6-10 ('devote to destruction'); the vow makes the cities *ḥērem*, the noun of 18:14 'devoted thing' (`cherem-devoted-thing-utterly-destroy-numbers`). The Moabite Mesha stele uses the same verb for the devotion of Nebo (line 17).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וַיַּחֲרֵ֥ם אֶתְהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־עָרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א שֵׁם־הַמָּק֖וֹם חָרְמָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And YHWH listened to the voice of Yisra'el and gave up the Canaanite; and they devoted them and their cities to destruction; and the name of the place was called Chormah.

notes.official: *wayyišmaʿ YHWH bəqôl yiśrāʾēl* 'And YHWH listened to the voice of Yisra'el'. *wayyaḥărēm ʾeṯhem* 'and they devoted them ... to destruction' (draft and ASV 'utterly destroyed'; singular verb with a collective subject; `cherem-devoted-thing-utterly-destroy-numbers`). *wayyiqrāʾ šem-hammāqôm ḥormâ* 'and the name of the place was called Chormah' (ASV Hormah): the name plays on the verb *ḥrm* of the same verse, and with 'devoted ... to destruction' in the line the wordplay is visible to an English reader; the text does not state the etymology in a causal clause, so the name is not glossed (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`; `cherem-devoted-thing-utterly-destroy-numbers`; cf. 14:45; Judg 1:17).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֞וּ מֵהֹ֤ר הָהָר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם־ס֔וּף לִסְבֹ֖ב אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נֶֽפֶשׁ־הָעָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Mount Hor by the way to the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom; and the people became impatient because of the way.

notes.official: *wayyisʿû mēhōr hāhār* 'And they journeyed from Mount Hor', literally 'Hor the mountain' (20:22-29). *dereḵ yam-sûp̄* 'by the way to the Sea of Reeds' (central `yam-suf-sea-of-reeds-vs-red-sea-geographical-textual-cross-corpus`; ASV 'the Red Sea'), here the route toward the Gulf of Aqaba, to go around Edom (20:14-21; central `eretz`). *wattiqṣar nep̄eš-hāʿām baddāreḵ* 'and the people became impatient because of the way' (draft 'the soul of the people grew impatient'; ASV 'the soul of the people was much discouraged'): literally 'the nefesh of the people grew short', an idiom of impatience (Judg 16:16; Zech 11:8), rendered by its sense under `nefesh-scope-torah`.

paragraphs.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר הָעָ֗ם בֵּֽאלֹהִים֮ וּבְמֹשֶׁה֒ לָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֙נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לָמ֖וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לֶ֙חֶם֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְנַפְשֵׁ֣נוּ קָ֔צָה בַּלֶּ֖חֶם הַקְּלֹקֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And the people spoke against the Elohim and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Mitsrayim to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread and there is no water, and we loathe this worthless bread."

notes.official: *wayḏabbēr hāʿām bēʾlōhîm ûḇəmōšeh* 'And the people spoke against the Elohim and against Moses': the article follows `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-torah` (central `elohim-as-translation`), and the plural verb *heʿĕlîṯunû* 'have you brought us up' addresses both. *wənap̄šēnû qāṣâ* 'and we loathe' (draft 'our soul loathes'; ASV 'our soul loatheth'): the *nep̄eš* is the speakers themselves (`nefesh-scope-torah`). *ballēḥem haqqəlōqēl* 'this worthless bread', the manna; *qəlōqēl* (only here) is from *qll* 'be light, contemptible' (ASV 'light bread'; NJPS 'this miserable food'). *mimmiṣrayim* 'out of Mitsrayim' (central `mitsrayim`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וַֽיְנַשְּׁכ֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֥מָת עַם־רָ֖ב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And YHWH sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and many people of Yisra'el died.

notes.official: *wayšallaḥ YHWH bāʿām ʾēṯ hannəḥāšîm haśśərāp̄îm* 'And YHWH sent fiery serpents among the people' (ASV). *śārāp̄*, from *śrp* 'burn', describes the serpents, perhaps by the burning of the bite or by their colour; the same noun names the 'flying *śārāp̄*' of Isa 14:29; 30:6 and the winged *śərāp̄îm* of Isa 6:2 (new overlay `saraf-fiery-serpent-numbers-21`; NJPS 'seraph serpents'; Joines, *JBL* 86, 1967). The article presents the serpents as known (cf. Deut 8:15).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי־דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ הִתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלֵ֖ינוּ אֶת־הַנָּחָ֑שׁ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד הָעָֽם׃

i18n.en: And the people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, for we have spoken against YHWH and against you; pray to YHWH, that he take away the serpents from us." And Moses prayed for the people.

notes.official: *wəyāsēr mēʿālênû ʾeṯ-hannāḥāš* 'that he take away the serpents from us': the Hebrew has the collective singular 'the serpent', and the line follows the ASV plural (`saraf-fiery-serpent-numbers-21`). *hiṯpallēl* 'pray': Moses intercedes as at 11:2 and 14:13-19.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף וְשִׂ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ עַל־נֵ֑ס וְהָיָה֙ כָּל־הַנָּשׁ֔וּךְ וְרָאָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ וָחָֽי׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Make yourself a fiery serpent and set it upon a standard; and it shall come to pass that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live."

notes.official:
*ʿăśēh ləḵā śārāp̄* 'Make yourself a fiery serpent': the Hebrew has only the noun *śārāp̄*, 'a burning one'; the ASV supplies 'serpent', and the line does the same, since v 9 identifies the object as a *nāḥāš* (`saraf-fiery-serpent-numbers-21`; NJPS 'a seraph figure'). *wəśîm ʾōṯô ʿal-nēs* 'and set it upon a standard': *nēs* is a signal pole or banner (Isa 5:26; 11:12; exodus-woh 17:15 'YHWH is my banner'); ASV 'standard', NRSV 'pole'. *wərāʾâ ʾōṯô wāḥāy* 'when he sees it, shall live'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live!') and reads the episode as the creators teaching men to give injections against snakebite. The line renders *śārāp̄* and *nēs* by their lexical senses and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מֹשֶׁה֙ נְחַ֣שׁ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וַיְשִׂמֵ֖הוּ עַל־הַנֵּ֑ס וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־נָשַׁ֤ךְ הַנָּחָשׁ֙ אֶת־אִ֔ישׁ וְהִבִּ֛יט אֶל־נְחַ֥שׁ הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת וָחָֽי׃

i18n.en: And Moses made a serpent of bronze and set it upon the standard; and it came to pass that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked to the serpent of bronze, he lived.

notes.official:
*nəḥaš nəḥōšeṯ* 'a serpent of bronze' (draft and ASV 'brass'): the Hebrew plays on *nāḥāš* 'serpent' and *nəḥōšeṯ* 'bronze, copper', and 'bronze' follows the new central `nechoshet-bronze-copper-alloy-cross-corpus` (as 1-kings-woh 8:64 and NRSV; NJPS 'a copper serpent'). The object was kept until Chizqiyahu destroyed it under the name Nechushtan (2 Kgs 18:4). Copper serpents have been found at Timna, in a shrine of the twelfth century BCE, and at Hazor and Megiddo (Rothenberg, *Timna*, 1972; Joines, *JBL* 87, 1968). *wəhibbîṭ ʾel-nəḥaš hannəḥōšeṯ* 'when he looked to the serpent of bronze': *hibbîṭ* is to look intently. Wis 16:5-7 and Jn 3:14-15 reinterpret the scene.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) refers to this verse when it says that the bitten man 'looked at' the 'serpent of brass' (French *serpent d'airain*) while a syringe was brought to him and he received an injection of serum. The canon's English follows the KJV 'brass'; the line uses 'bronze' for the metal under the central entry, and the reading is recorded here only.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאֹבֹֽת׃

i18n.en: And the children of Yisra'el journeyed and camped in Ovot.

notes.official: Ovot (ASV Oboth; also 33:43-44). The itinerary of vv 10-20 runs from the edge of Edom northward to the plateau of Moab; on its relation to the fuller list of ch. 33 see G. I. Davies, *The Way of the Wilderness* (1979).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֹבֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֞וּ בְּעִיֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבָרִ֗ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב מִמִּזְרַ֖ח הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: And they journeyed from Ovot and camped at Iyye-ha'Avarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrise.

notes.official: *ʿiyyê hāʿăḇārîm* Iyye-ha'Avarim (ASV Iye-abarim), 'the ruins of the Avarim'. *mimmizraḥ haššāmeš* 'toward the sunrise', i.e. on the east side of Moab.

paragraphs.text: מִשָּׁ֖ם נָסָ֑עוּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּנַ֥חַל זָֽרֶד׃

i18n.en: From there they journeyed and camped in the valley of Zered.

notes.official: *naḥal zāreḏ* 'the valley of Zered' (ASV): *naḥal* is a wadi, a seasonal stream-bed (Wadi el-Hesa), the border between Edom and Moab.

paragraphs.text: מִשָּׁם֮ נָסָעוּ֒ וַֽיַּחֲנ֗וּ מֵעֵ֤בֶר אַרְנוֹן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר הַיֹּצֵ֖א מִגְּב֣וּל הָֽאֱמֹרִ֑י כִּ֤י אַרְנוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב בֵּ֥ין מוֹאָ֖ב וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

i18n.en: From there they journeyed and camped on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness that comes out from the border of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

notes.official: *mēʿēḇer ʾarnôn* 'on the other side of the Arnon' (Wadi Mujib), the northern border of Moab. *hāʾĕmōrî* 'the Amorites', a collective singular in Hebrew, takes the English gentilic under `hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`.

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּן֙ יֵֽאָמַ֔ר בְּסֵ֖פֶר מִלְחֲמֹ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אֶת־וָהֵ֣ב בְּסוּפָ֔ה וְאֶת־הַנְּחָלִ֖ים אַרְנֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of YHWH: "Vahev in Sufah, and the valleys of the Arnon,

notes.official: *bəsēp̄er milḥămōṯ YHWH* 'in the Book of the Wars of YHWH', a lost collection of war poetry, comparable to the Book of Yashar (Josh 10:13; 2 Sam 1:18). The quotation *ʾeṯ-wāhēḇ bəsûp̄â wəʾeṯ-hannəḥālîm ʾarnôn* begins with the object marker and has no verb: it is a fragment. *wāhēḇ* and *sûp̄â* are taken as place names (ASV 'Vaheb in Suphah'), although *sûp̄â* is also 'storm-wind' ('Waheb in a storm'; Christensen, *CBQ* 36, 1974). The line keeps the ASV reading and the incompleteness of the Hebrew (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *hannəḥālîm* 'the valleys', the wadis of the Arnon. The quotation runs to v 15 (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֶ֙שֶׁד֙ הַנְּחָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָ֖ה לְשֶׁ֣בֶת עָ֑ר וְנִשְׁעַ֖ן לִגְב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃

i18n.en: and the slope of the valleys that turns toward the dwelling of Ar and leans upon the border of Moab."

notes.official: *wəʾešeḏ hannəḥālîm* 'and the slope of the valleys': *ʾešeḏ* is a slope or watercourse (Deut 3:17; 4:49 'the slopes of Pisgah'). *šeḇeṯ ʿār* 'the dwelling of Ar', the Moabite city or district of Ar (v 28; Deut 2:9).

paragraphs.text: וּמִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֑רָה הִ֣וא הַבְּאֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה אֱסֹף֙ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם מָֽיִם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And from there to Be'er: that is the well of which YHWH said to Moses, "Gather the people, and I will give them water."

notes.official: *ûmiššām bəʾērâ hiwʾ habbəʾēr* 'And from there to Be'er: that is the well': the place name *bəʾēr* means 'well', and the text supplies the explanation itself, so no gloss is added (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-torah`). The ASV supplies '[they went]'; the line follows the verbless Hebrew. *ʾĕsōp̄ ʾeṯ-hāʿām wəʾettənâ lāhem māyim* 'Gather the people, and I will give them water'.

paragraphs.text: אָ֚ז יָשִׁ֣יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־הַשִּׁירָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עֲלִ֥י בְאֵ֖ר עֱנוּ־לָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Then Yisra'el sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing to it!

notes.official: *ʾāz yāšîr yiśrāʾēl* 'Then Yisra'el sang', the formula of Ex 15:1. *ʿălî ḇəʾēr ʿĕnû-lāh* 'Spring up, O well! Sing to it!': the Song of the Well (vv 17-18) is a work song, perhaps sung at the opening of a well (Levine 2000). The song takes double marks (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: בְּאֵ֞ר חֲפָר֣וּהָ שָׂרִ֗ים כָּר֙וּהָ֙ נְדִיבֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם בִּמְחֹקֵ֖ק בְּמִשְׁעֲנֹתָ֑ם וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר מַתָּנָֽה׃

i18n.en: The well, which the princes dug, which the nobles of the people delved, with the scepter, with their staffs." And from the wilderness to Mattanah;

notes.official: *bimḥōqēq bəmišʿănōṯām* 'with the scepter, with their staffs': *məḥōqēq* is a ruler's staff (Gen 49:10; ASV 'the sceptre') or 'the lawgiver' (Rashi), and the nobles dig ceremonially with their staffs of office. *ûmimmiḏbār mattānâ* 'And from the wilderness to Mattanah': the itinerary resumes inside the verse, as the MT divides it; the LXX reads 'and from the well (*bəʾēr*) to Mattanah' (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *mattānâ* is also 'gift', and the Targums read the names of vv 18-19 as a midrash on a well that followed Israel (Tg. Onqelos; cf. 1 Cor 10:4).

paragraphs.text: וּמִמַּתָּנָ֖ה נַחֲלִיאֵ֑ל וּמִנַּחֲלִיאֵ֖ל בָּמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: and from Mattanah to Nachali'el; and from Nachali'el to Bamot;

notes.official: Nachali'el (ASV Nahaliel), 'wadi of El'; Bamot (ASV Bamoth), 'high places', perhaps the Bamot-Ba'al of 22:41 and the *bt bmt* of the Mesha stele (line 27).

paragraphs.text: וּמִבָּמ֗וֹת הַגַּיְא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה וְנִשְׁקָ֖פָה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן׃ (פ)

i18n.en: and from Bamot to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down upon the desert.

notes.official: *hayšîmōn* 'the desert' (ASV): a common noun 'wasteland', or the place name Yeshimon (cf. Beit-haYeshimot, 33:49); the article favours the common noun. *biśḏēh môʾāḇ* 'in the field of Moab', i.e. its territory. From Pisgah Moses later views the land (Deut 3:27; 34:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־סִיחֹ֥ן מֶֽלֶךְ־הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el sent messengers to Sichon king of the Amorites, saying,

notes.official: *wayyišlaḥ yiśrāʾēl malʾāḵîm* 'And Yisra'el sent messengers', as to Edom (20:14). Sichon (ASV Sihon), 'king of the Amorites' (Deut 2:26-37; Judg 11:19-22).

paragraphs.text: אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם לֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר־נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: "Let me pass through your land; we will not turn aside into field or into vineyard; we will not drink the water of the wells; we will go by the king's highway until we have passed through your border."

notes.official: *bəḏereḵ hammeleḵ* 'by the king's highway', the north-south road of Transjordan (20:17). *bəʾarṣeḵā* 'through your land' (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹא־נָתַ֨ן סִיחֹ֣ן אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻלוֹ֒ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף סִיחֹ֜ן אֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֗וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֞א לִקְרַ֤את יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּדְבָּ֔רָה וַיָּבֹ֖א יָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: But Sichon would not allow Yisra'el to pass through his border; and Sichon gathered all his people and went out against Yisra'el into the wilderness, and came to Yahatz; and he fought against Yisra'el.

notes.official: *yāhṣâ* 'to Yahatz' (ASV Jahaz), with the directional ending; the town is named on the Mesha stele (lines 18-20, *yhṣ*).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וַיִּירַ֨שׁ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ מֵֽאַרְנֹ֗ן עַד־יַבֹּק֙ עַד־בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֣י עַ֔ז גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el struck him with the edge of the sword and possessed his land from the Arnon to the Yabboq, as far as the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.

notes.official: *ləp̄î-ḥāreḇ* 'with the edge of the sword', literally 'the mouth'. *mēʾarnōn ʿaḏ-yabbōq* 'from the Arnon to the Yabboq' (ASV Jabbok). *kî ʿaz gəḇûl bənê ʿammôn* 'for the border of the children of Ammon was strong' (MT, ASV); the LXX reads *yaʿzēr* 'Jazer' for *ʿaz*, anticipating v 32 (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *ʾarṣô* 'his land' (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ת כָּל־הֶעָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּכָל־עָרֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וּבְכָל־בְּנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Yisra'el took all these cities, and Yisra'el dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Cheshbon and in all its towns.

notes.official: Cheshbon (ASV Heshbon). *ûḇəḵol-bənōṯêhā* 'and in all its towns', literally 'its daughters', the dependent villages.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן עִ֗יר סִיחֹ֛ן מֶ֥לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י הִ֑וא וְה֣וּא נִלְחַ֗ם בְּמֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־כָּל־אַרְצ֛וֹ מִיָּד֖וֹ עַד־אַרְנֹֽן׃

i18n.en: For Cheshbon was the city of Sichon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land out of his hand, as far as the Arnon.

notes.official: The verse explains that Sichon had taken Cheshbon from Moab, which prepares the song of vv 27-30 (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: עַל־כֵּ֛ן יֹאמְר֥וּ הַמֹּשְׁלִ֖ים בֹּ֣אוּ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן תִּבָּנֶ֥ה וְתִכּוֹנֵ֖ן עִ֥יר סִיחֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Therefore those who speak in proverbs say, "Come to Cheshbon! Let the city of Sichon be built and established!

notes.official: *hammōšəlîm* 'those who speak in proverbs' (ASV), from *māšāl* 'saying, taunt'; NJPS 'the bards', NRSV 'the ballad singers'. The Cheshbon song (vv 27-30) is a taunt song; whether it celebrates Sichon's victory over Moab or Israel's over Sichon is debated (Hanson, *HTR* 61, 1968; Levine 2000). The song takes double marks (`direct-speech-quotation-marks-convention-torah`).

paragraphs.text: כִּי־אֵשׁ֙ יָֽצְאָ֣ה מֵֽחֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן לֶהָבָ֖ה מִקִּרְיַ֣ת סִיחֹ֑ן אָֽכְלָה֙ עָ֣ר מוֹאָ֔ב בַּעֲלֵ֖י בָּמ֥וֹת אַרְנֹֽן׃

i18n.en: For a fire has gone out from Cheshbon, a flame from the city of Sichon; it has devoured Ar of Moab, the lords of the high places of the Arnon.

notes.official: *kî-ʾēš yāṣəʾâ mēḥešbôn* 'For a fire has gone out from Cheshbon' (reused at Jer 48:45). *baʿălê bāmôṯ ʾarnōn* 'the lords of the high places of the Arnon' (MT, ASV); the LXX reads *bālʿâ* 'it swallowed' for *baʿălê*, giving a parallel to 'it devoured' (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). *bāmôṯ* may also be the place name of v 19.

paragraphs.text: אוֹי־לְךָ֣ מוֹאָ֔ב אָבַ֖דְתָּ עַם־כְּמ֑וֹשׁ נָתַ֨ן בָּנָ֤יו פְּלֵיטִם֙ וּבְנֹתָ֣יו בַּשְּׁבִ֔ית לְמֶ֥לֶךְ אֱמֹרִ֖י סִיחֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Woe to you, Moab! You are undone, O people of Kemosh! He has given his sons as fugitives and his daughters into captivity, to Sichon king of the Amorites.

notes.official: *ʿam-kəmôš* 'O people of Kemosh' (ASV Chemosh), the national god of Moab (Judg 11:24; 1 Kgs 11:7; *kmš* on the Mesha stele). *nāṯan bānāyw pəlêṭim* 'He has given his sons as fugitives': Kemosh has abandoned his people (cf. Jer 48:46).

paragraphs.text: וַנִּירָ֛ם אָבַ֥ד חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן עַד־דִּיב֑וֹן וַנַּשִּׁ֣ים עַד־נֹ֔פַח אֲשֶׁ֖רׄ עַד־מֵֽידְבָֽא׃

i18n.en: We have shot at them; Cheshbon has perished as far as Dibon, and we have laid waste as far as Nofach, which reaches to Medeva."

notes.official: *wannîrām ʾāḇaḏ ḥešbôn ʿaḏ-dîḇôn* 'We have shot at them; Cheshbon has perished as far as Dibon': *wannîrām* is read as 'we shot them' (*yrh*, ASV), or as *nîrām* 'their dominion' (the Samaritan and the LXX, 'their seed'). The word *ʾăšer* near the end carries a Masoretic extraordinary point over its *rēš*, one of the ten *nĕqûdôt* of the Torah (Sifre Num 69), which marks the reading as doubtful; the Samaritan Pentateuch and the LXX read *ʾēš* 'fire' ('with fire as far as Medeva'), which many commentators adopt. The line translates the MT as the ASV does ('which reaches to Medeva') and records the point here (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). Nofach (ASV Nophah) and Medeva (ASV Medeba).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֙שֶׁב֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּאֶ֖רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִֽי׃

i18n.en: Thus Yisra'el dwelt in the land of the Amorites.

notes.official: *wayyēšeḇ yiśrāʾēl bəʾereṣ hāʾĕmōrî* 'Thus Yisra'el dwelt in the land of the Amorites' (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח מֹשֶׁה֙ לְרַגֵּ֣ל אֶת־יַעְזֵ֔ר וַֽיִּלְכְּד֖וּ בְּנֹתֶ֑יהָ ויירש [וַיּ֖וֹרֶשׁ] אֶת־הָאֱמֹרִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And Moses sent to spy out Ya'zer; and they took its towns and drove out the Amorites who were there.

notes.official: *wayyōreš ʾeṯ-hāʾĕmōrî ʾăšer-šām* 'and drove out the Amorites who were there': the Qere *wayyôreš* is a Hiphil singular, 'he dispossessed'; the Ketiv *wyyrš* has no final *waw* and can only be the singular Qal *wayyîraš* 'and he took possession of'. The line translates the Qere; the plural subject it keeps, with the ASV, comes from the preceding *wayyilkədû* 'they took' and from the LXX *exebalon* 'they drove out', not from the Ketiv (`mt-baseline-ketiv-qere-and-accent-division-torah`). Ya'zer (ASV Jazer).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְנוּ֙ וַֽיַּעֲל֔וּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתָ֜ם ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃

i18n.en: And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan; and Og king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edre'i.

notes.official: Og king of Bashan, the last of the Refa'im (Deut 3:11). Edre'i (ASV Edrei).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Moses, "Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Cheshbon."

notes.official: *ʾal-tîrāʾ ʾōṯô* 'Do not fear him' (central `al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`). Here the motive clause is *kî ḇəyāḏəḵā nāṯattî ʾōṯô* 'for into your hand I have given him', the form of the war oracle (Josh 8:1; 10:8), rather than the presence formula 'for I am with you'; the perfect *nāṯattî* treats the outcome as already settled. *ʾarṣô* 'his land' (central `eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ וְאֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת־אַרְצֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: So they struck him and his sons and all his people, until there was no survivor left to him; and they possessed his land.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ-biltî hišʾîr-lô śārîḏ* 'until there was no survivor left to him'. Deut 2:26-3:11 retells the defeat of Sichon and Og (central `eretz`).
